title: Quasi-finiteness along the finite component of a fibre
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite-type map of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and suppose $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$. Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)$, viewed as the corresponding closed-and-open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ over $V(I)$. Then $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $B$ belonging to $T$, in the affine sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (Stacks Algebra, Definition 10.122.3, Tag 00PL; its isolated-fibre criterion is Tag 00PK and the finite-fibre criterion used here is Tag 00PM).

source.place: literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type): quasi-finite at every prime of T by looking at fibre rings; the affine definition/criterion are Algebra Tags 00PK and 00PM
